ZAF.hook: Has three capital cities at once — Pretoria governs, Cape Town legislates, Bloemfontein judges — and twelve official languages.
ZAF.place: The bottom of the continent, completely surrounding Lesotho and wrapping around Eswatini.
ZAF.borders: The 1910 Union stitched two British colonies and two Boer republics inside their outer limits — completely surrounding Lesotho; on the Namibian border the line sits on the Orange river's north bank rather than midstream, a colonial quirk Namibia still contests.

NAM.hook: The Namib is the oldest desert on Earth at around 55 million years, and its Skeleton Coast is littered with shipwrecks.
NAM.place: On the Atlantic between Angola and South Africa, with the Caprivi Strip reaching east toward the Zambezi.
NAM.borders: German South-West Africa's box — including the Caprivi Strip, a 450 km corridor Germany extracted in an 1890 treaty hoping to reach the Zambezi and the Indian Ocean, apparently not reckoning with Victoria Falls in between.

BWA.hook: The Okavango spills into the Kalahari and simply evaporates — one of the few great river deltas that never reaches the sea.
BWA.place: Landlocked above South Africa, between Namibia and Zimbabwe.
BWA.borders: The Bechuanaland Protectorate's lines: the Molopo and Limpopo rivers plus long survey lines through the Kalahari, meeting three neighbours at Kazungula on the Zambezi — a near-four-corners point now spanned by a bridge.

LSO.hook: One of only three countries entirely surrounded by a single other country — and its lowest point, at 1,400m, is the highest low point on Earth.
LSO.place: Entirely inside South Africa, up in the Drakensberg mountains.
LSO.borders: The mountain kingdom of Moshoeshoe I, who accepted British protection in 1868 to halt Boer encroachment — at the price of the western lowlands, leaving a state entirely surrounded by what became South Africa.

SWZ.hook: Renamed itself from Swaziland in 2018, partly because it kept being confused with Switzerland — and it remains one of the world's last absolute monarchies.
SWZ.place: A small landlocked kingdom between South Africa and Mozambique.
SWZ.borders: The Swazi kingdom's core, kept as a British protectorate rather than absorbed — though 19th-century concessions trimmed it, and the modern state still claims Swazi lands lying inside South Africa.
